items.title: Code: agent/src/internal: ModelStep.ts L315-633
items.why: ModelStep, the durable model call; read this first; landed today; guide attached
items.context:
# Model step: recording a live attempt

## What
This collects a model answer, reports live events and records the final answer or a terminal model error. It also preserves the reported spend from failed attempts without replaying their partial text.

## Why
Completed calls must replay and transient failures must remain retryable. [Decision 0011](apps/mvp/docs/decisions/0011-the-agent-runs-in-the-browser.md) §3 supplies that requirement; the separate harness retry ladder is an implementation choice, explained in this file, rather than a product decision.

## How
- `recordModelStep` accepts either a Schedule or `"engine"`; engine mode disables local retries and transport executor retries.
- The local schedule filters error codes before emitting retry events, preventing phantom retries for terminal failures.
- Every attempt, event and transport keep-alive feeds the action heartbeat; local idle detection instead watches events.
- An overrun interrupts the attempt; local mode may reissue with one teaching note derived from the original request.
- A stream ending without `settle` becomes a transport failure. Capacity failures remain unsealed.
- Failed attempts contribute their final cumulative usage once; only the final attempt contributes answer text.

## Architecture diagram
```text
Harness or public ModelStep dispatch
             | request + policy
             v
 +----------------------------------+
 | [THIS] recorder                  |
 | attempt -> heartbeat -> collect  |
 | retry marker / usage aggregation |
 +----------------------------------+
      | Model.stream          | events + error
      v                       v
 injected route          sealed Action journal
 browser -> Worker proxy -> provider
 other hosts -> configured provider route
```

## Read this first
- `packages/smithers/agent/src/internal/ModelStep.ts:435` — entry point selects the retry owner.
- `packages/smithers/agent/src/internal/ModelStep.ts:517` — transport retries and liveness are injected at the stream boundary.
- `packages/smithers/agent/src/internal/ModelStep.ts:578` — truncated success becomes transport failure.
- `packages/smithers/agent/src/internal/ModelStep.ts:607` — failed usage is folded into the saved answer.

## Questions a reviewer should ask
- Do retry events reach live consumers before any replacement answer event?
- Does interrupted or rejected work retain its usage exactly once?
- Could teaching on a local retry break the prompt-cache assumption documented for public engine mode?

files.note: `recordModelStep`: retries inside the sealed step, overrun teaching, a heartbeat per event. Check that a `retry` event reaches `onEvent` before a new attempt's events, and that usage sums correctly across attempts.

items.why: @smthrs/flow, the flow core; read this first; landed recently; guide attached
items.context:
# Action construction: schemas and declarations

## What
This builds the values that describe and execute one durable action. Named declarations can enter a flow plan before a host supplies their implementation.

## Why
[Decision 0003](apps/mvp/docs/decisions/0003-flows-and-the-agent.md) establishes shared flows for people and agents, and [decision 0011](apps/mvp/docs/decisions/0011-the-agent-runs-in-the-browser.md) §6 requires host-independent code. DUR-1 places effects inside durable steps; the library catalog names `Action.make` for that job.

## How
- Exit codecs are cached by success/error schema identity, so repeated dispatches reuse compiled parser ASTs.
- Inline actions carry schemas, tier, identity, retry policy, file boundary and attempt bounds.
- Execution encoding preserves cleanup failures beside interruption by turning typed cleanup reasons into defects.
- Declared actions normalize the payload schema and lower capability/effect literals into annotations.
- Annotated copies avoid lowering literals twice, so explicit annotation overrides survive.
- Each named declaration mints a requirement service and `.call()` produces a planned action node.

## Architecture diagram
```text
App/plugin Flow body
       | declared Action.call(payload)
       v
 @smthrs/flow [THIS] Action.make
       | node + schemas + capability/effect ceiling
       v
 Graph -> Interpreter -> implementation layer
                            | inline Action
                            v
                       FlowRuntime -> host journal
 browser / Worker / sandbox host supplies effects
 (this constructor opens no network or database connection)
```

## Read this first
- `packages/smithers/flows/flow/src/Action/make.ts:51` — schema cache assumes schema identities are stable.
- `packages/smithers/flows/flow/src/Action/make.ts:188` — timeout wrapper encloses infrastructure recovery.
- `packages/smithers/flows/flow/src/Action/make.ts:233` — interruption cleanup failures must survive encoding.
- `packages/smithers/flows/flow/src/Action/make.ts:275` — declaration lowering and annotation precedence.

## Questions a reviewer should ask
- Are codec cache entries safe if callers mutate schema objects?
- Can annotation copies accidentally change authority or identity?
- Why do the plan deep imports at lines 9–10 still violate SDK-5?

files.note: Marked human-reviewed 2026-08-10. Durable action construction: exit schemas, tiers, implementation version checks, attempt timeouts. Uses deep imports (`@smthrs/plan/Node`, `@smthrs/plan/Effects`) that the root-imports rule bans.

items.title: Code: flows/flow/test: Interpreter.test.ts L321-640
items.why: @smthrs/flow, the flow core; landed today; guide attached
items.context:
## What
These tests separate recoverable action failures from interpreter refusals.
They also test joined results, unresolved references and ambiguous graph identities.

## Why
One flow model needs predictable execution and useful failures before effects escape.
See `apps/mvp/docs/decisions/0014-flows-authoring-debugging-and-home-view.md`
decision 1 and `packages/smithers/flows/flow/docs/testing.md`. Catalog: `@smthrs/flow`.
These are authoring-package fixture tests, not production engine conformance evidence.

## How
- A detached inline call must remain an interpreter refusal even inside an unfiltered catch.
- Schema-matched failures enter recovery; unmatched errors keep their original values.
- Constant failures use the same catch rules as action failures, including empty strings.
- Nested catches preserve failed-node bookkeeping and skipped recovery arms.
- Node.all joins by member name and preserves own __proto__ values without prototype mutation.
- Unknown reference targets, missing implementations and duplicate node ids are refused explicitly.

## Architecture diagram
```text
Test-built catch / join / reference graph
                    |
 [THIS: recovery + join + identity assertions]
                    | Interpreter.interpret
                    v
       graph validation -> interpreter walk -> fixture action dispatch
             |                    |                    |
             +-- typed refusal    +-- settled/failed/skipped maps
                                      |
                                 value assertions
Entirely in-process; external storage and host boundaries are not exercised.
```

## Read this first
- `packages/smithers/flows/flow/test/Interpreter.test.ts:321` — an interpreter refusal must bypass an ordinary recovery arm.
- `packages/smithers/flows/flow/test/Interpreter.test.ts:419` — an empty-string failure must survive schema rejection.
- `packages/smithers/flows/flow/test/Interpreter.test.ts:544` — a reference to an earlier graph cannot dispatch this graph.
- `packages/smithers/flows/flow/test/Interpreter.test.ts:603` — dotted names can create duplicate durable node addresses.

## Questions a reviewer should ask
- Does refusing duplicate ids happen before every possible action effect?
- Do nested catches preserve the original error when a schema does not match?
- Where are join cancellation and concurrent failures tested beyond this range?

files.note: Look at: behavior asserted through the public boundary; failure and ordering cases. Lines 321-640.

## What
This slice checks useful refusals for broken or detached flow bodies. It also pins the
rule that a flow has one body, then sets up fixtures for concurrency tests that follow.

## Why
One flow model needs predictable execution and useful failures before effects escape.
See `apps/mvp/docs/decisions/0014-flows-authoring-debugging-and-home-view.md`
decision 1 and `packages/smithers/flows/flow/docs/testing.md`. Catalog: `@smthrs/flow`.
These are authoring-package fixture tests, not production engine conformance evidence.

## How
- Thrown Errors and bare values become incomplete_graph errors with useful context.
- Accessor-backed thrown data must not execute getters while formatting a refusal.
- Missing implementations and detached maps are rejected before an earlier action can run.
- Detached inline calls and handoffs cannot run without their required declarations.
- Type and runtime assertions prohibit a flow toLayer handler, including after annotation.
- The final section defines parking/release/failure services; its overlap assertions are outside this slice.

## Architecture diagram
```text
Throwing / detached body         Public Flow declaration
            |                            |
            v                            v
 [THIS: refusal assertions]     [THIS: body-only surface assertions]
            |                            |
            +--------> real Interpreter <+
                            |
                  local runtime + action table
                            |
              typed errors / calls / annotation behavior
Concurrency fixture: Parking waits <- Release; Failing returns a typed error.
No deployed host, external database, sandbox or provider is involved.
```

## Read this first
- `packages/smithers/flows/flow/test/Interpreter.test.ts:686` — error formatting must leave accessor-backed thrown data inert.
- `packages/smithers/flows/flow/test/Interpreter.test.ts:720` — half-wired graph must fail before the implemented Read runs.
- `packages/smithers/flows/flow/test/Interpreter.test.ts:800` — body-only behavior is asserted in both types and JavaScript.
- `packages/smithers/flows/flow/test/Interpreter.test.ts:901` — parking helper establishes a dependency; overlap tests follow after line 952.

## Questions a reviewer should ask
- Can hostile thrown objects still invoke traps during fallback formatting?
- Do all annotation paths preserve the exact body while exposing no second handler?
- Do the later concurrency tests have a deadline so a sequential regression fails promptly?

items.title: Code: flows/flow/src/internal: OutcomeMarker.ts, RecordedPlan.ts, SpanFailure.ts
items.why: @smthrs/flow, the flow core; landed recently; guide attached
items.context:
# Outcome markers, restart compatibility and safe span failures

## What
These helpers distinguish authored flow outcomes, compare rebuilt plans after restart and withhold error text from tracing. They preserve the caller’s original failure while changing only the span’s copy.

## Why
Restart identity must tolerate harmless bundle renaming without weakening cache identity, and traces must exclude content. See `apps/mvp/docs/decisions/0014-flows-authoring-debugging-and-home-view.md` and `0011-the-agent-runs-in-the-browser.md`; catalog entries: `@smthrs/flow`, `@smthrs/plan`.

## How
- Two symbols distinguish outcome AST nodes from resolved outcome values.
- RecordedPlan projects resumeDigest only in known callback slots.
- Missing resume identity retains the original material and fails closed.
- Approval digests and dispatch keys retain their stronger identity; this projection is resume-only.
- SpanFailure replaces failure/defect text with tag or class and a restricted code; interruptions pass through.
- Tracer wrappers are idempotent; effect, stream, function and one-span adapters preserve caller errors.

## Architecture diagram
```text
done / to / park -> [SLICE: OutcomeMarker] -> Graph / Interpreter
                                             |
 rebuilt graph -> [SLICE: RecordedPlan] -> PlanRecorded digest comparison
                                             | durable journal
 action / provider failure                    v
          | original cause ------------> caller / typed recovery
          |
          +-> [SLICE: SpanFailure] -> stand-in exit -> tracer / OTLP exporter
                   tag + restricted code; original message withheld
 Host: browser / Worker / sandbox; provider is outside this package
```

## Read this first
- `packages/smithers/flows/flow/src/internal/RecordedPlan.ts:31`: only callback slots may use weaker resume identity; never application data.
- `packages/smithers/flows/flow/src/internal/SpanFailure.ts:46`: tag is copied without validation; could an untrusted _tag carry private text?
- `packages/smithers/flows/flow/src/internal/SpanFailure.ts:66`: failure replacement retains cause annotations; inspect their content policy.
- `packages/smithers/flows/flow/src/internal/SpanFailure.ts:145`: withSpan sanitizes this span while nested spans keep the caller tracer.

## Questions a reviewer should ask
- Can weaker resume identity ever enter an approval digest or cache key?
- Are tags and cause annotations trusted enough to export without text filtering?
- Does wrapping a tracer leave every caller-visible failure unchanged?

files.note: The two markers that let `Flow.isOutcome` tell an authored `done`/`to`/`park` from ordinary data. Exports `OutcomeNodeTypeId`, `OutcomeValueTypeId`. Look at: correctness, naming and whether it can be smaller.
Resume compatibility is weaker than result reuse. Exports `recordedPlanDrafts`. Look at: deep import (root entries only).
Span failures with their text withheld. Exports `exit`, `tracer`, `effect`, `stream`, `fn` +1. Look at: correctness, naming and whether it can be smaller.

items.title: Code: flows/flow/src/Flow: Annotations.ts, CapabilityCeiling.ts, DeadlineExce...
items.context:
# Flow policies and authority ceilings

## What
These types describe where a flow runs, what it may touch, and how failures are represented. The helpers intersect permissions so a nested flow cannot gain authority from its caller.

## Why
Decision `apps/mvp/docs/decisions/0003-flows-and-the-agent.md` puts placement and authority on shared declarations. DUR-1 requires the engine to retain execution identity and deadlines. Catalog entry: `@smthrs/flow`; package docs: `docs/concepts/the-runtime-port.md`.

## How
- Annotations reuse the plan package’s effect and placement models rather than copying them.
- An absent capability annotation inherits authority; an explicit empty pattern list denies everything.
- Transported ceilings are groups: groups intersect, while patterns within one group offer alternatives.
- Invalid patterns are dropped; an empty group therefore denies rather than opening authority.
- `ceilingWithin` accepts only provable containment; defect capture and model visibility default to true.
- `DeadlineExceeded` and `ExecutionIdRequired` define serializable defects; these files do not enforce timers or allocate identities.

## Architecture diagram
```text
Flow declaration + parent authority (any host)
                 | annotations / transported ceiling groups
                 v
     +---------------------------------------------+
     | [THIS SLICE] policies + ceiling intersection |
     | deadline / missing-identity defect schemas   |
     +---------------------------------------------+
            | narrower authority       | placement
            v                          v
     Interpreter / engine          host selection
            | injected services        |
            +------------+-------------+
                         v
       browser worker / Worker / sandbox host
       storage and network effects happen downstream
```

## Read this first
- `packages/smithers/flows/flow/src/Flow/CapabilityCeiling.ts:17` — Annotation presence distinguishes inheritance from denial.
- `packages/smithers/flows/flow/src/Flow/CapabilityCeiling.ts:50` — Intersection must never widen either side.
- `packages/smithers/flows/flow/src/Flow/Annotations.ts:127` — Model visibility defaults to yes; sensitive flows must opt out.

## Questions a reviewer should ask
- Do serialization and catalog projection preserve absent versus explicitly empty ceilings?
- Are all sensitive declarations explicitly hidden from models?
- Do the deep package imports satisfy the current root-entry rule?

files.note: Marked human-reviewed 2026-08-10; look at what changed since. Execution policies attached to flow definitions through Effect context. Exports `Effects`, `PlacementDirective`, `Capabilities`, `EffectsDeclaration`, `EffectEnvelope` +4. Look at: deep import (root entries only).

Declared capability ceilings shared by planning and execution. Exports `capabilityCeilings`, `parseCapabilityCeilings`, `attenuateCapabilities`, `intersectCeilings`, `ceilingWithin`. Look at: deep import (root entries only).
Defect recorded when an execution runs past its flow's declared deadline. Exports `DeadlineExceeded`. Look at: correctness, naming and whether it can be smaller.

Marked human-reviewed 2026-08-10; look at what changed since. Failure raised when a flow execution has no explicit or derived identity. Exports `ExecutionIdRequired`. Look at: correctness, naming and whether it can be smaller.

items.context:
# Clone progress in the feed; development identity

Slice: `code:mvp/worker/CloneFeed@aab5`
Coverage revision: `aab51be3bc62f0613f580f031902660930986b9e1e7ab4c73b33ff45bea79559`

## What
CloneFeed turns a repository's clone state into one notification for the person who requested the current attempt. This regrouped slice also includes the development-only API identity adapter and a helper that keeps error messages out of logs.

## Why
[0009](apps/mvp/docs/decisions/0009-notifications-and-live-work.md) makes notifications and toasts views of real progress. [0008](apps/mvp/docs/decisions/0008-auth.md) defines sign-in; the development fallback must stay outside production. Catalog entry: `@smthrs/notifications`.

## How
- fold joins clone_requests on repository and current clone_id; missing rows or an unnamed requester produce no notification.
- stateOf maps cloning stages to working and settled states to done or failed; old unstaged rows read as requested.
- The existing notification is locked; unchanged state/ref writes nothing, while renewed attention advances its version.
- The caller must include fold in the repository write transaction; the function itself does not open that transaction.
- DevChatApi reuses ChatApi.program with local role fixtures, local HTTP enabled and spend alerts disabled by default.
- codeOf emits SQL reason tags, other error tags or unknown; tests check messages are excluded and fold uses real Postgres.

## Architecture diagram
```text
Clone route / remote clone steps (Worker)
       | repository write, same transaction
       v
 Postgres repositories + clone_requests
       | current attempt + requester
       v
 [THIS: CloneFeed.fold] -> notifications -> Electric -> browser feed / toast
       |
       +--> state-only metric
Development entry (separate build)
 [THIS: DevChatApi] -> ChatApi.program -> same routes -> Postgres / model proxy
       | local person fixtures
Production entry -> ChatApi (must never select DevChatApi)
Failures -> [THIS: ErrorCode.codeOf] -> tag-only log fields
```

## Read this first
- `apps/mvp/worker/CloneFeed.ts:57` — Only the current clone attempt determines the recipient.
- `apps/mvp/worker/CloneFeed.ts:64` — Row lock protects existing entries; first insert still needs concurrency review.
- `apps/mvp/worker/DevChatApi.ts:60` — The development entry grants fallback authority and must not ship as production.
- `apps/mvp/worker/ErrorCode.ts:7` — Redaction trusts tags themselves to contain no user content.

## Questions a reviewer should ask
- Do all production fold callers share the repository write transaction, including failures?
- Can concurrent first folds overwrite a newer notification with an older state?
- What build check proves the development identity fallback cannot enter production?
